subject: Math
prompt:
$$k(t) = -4.9 t^{2} + 38 t + 6$$

The quadratic function shown models the height above the ground $k$, in meters, of a model rocket $t$ seconds after it was launched vertically upward. If $y = k(t)$ is graphed in the $ty$-plane, which of the following represents the real-life meaning of the positive $t$-intercept of the graph?

choices.A: The initial height of the rocket
choices.B: The maximum height of the rocket
choices.C: The time at which the rocket reaches its maximum height
choices.D: The time at which the rocket hits the ground

explanation: Choice D is correct. The positive $t$-intercept of the graph of $y = k(t)$ is a point $(t, y)$ for which $y = 0$. Since $y = k(t)$ models the height above the ground, in meters, of the rocket, a $y$-value of $0$ corresponds to the rocket being $0$ meters above the ground—that is, when the rocket is on the ground. Since $t$ represents the time since the rocket was launched, the positive $t$-intercept, $(t, 0)$, represents the time at which the rocket hits the ground.
